# Pigeons - complete documentation

> Open source email infrastructure for developers and AI agents.
> https://pigeons.dev

============================================================
Quick Start (quick-start)
============================================================

---
title: Quick Start
description: Get from zero to sending email in under 2 minutes.
---

## Start the server

```bash
docker run -d \
  -p 3891:3891 \
  -e PIGEONS_AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=your-key \
  -e PIGEONS_AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=your-secret \
  -e PIGEONS_AWS_REGION=us-east-1 \
  -e PIGEONS_FROM_EMAIL=noreply@yourdomain.com \
  ghcr.io/pigeons-dev/pigeons
```

On first boot, Pigeons prints your API key to stdout. Grab it from the logs:

```bash
docker logs $(docker ps -q --filter ancestor=ghcr.io/pigeons-dev/pigeons) 2>&1 | grep "Your API key"
```

The key starts with `pgn_`. Save it somewhere safe - it won't be shown again.

## Send your first email

```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:3891/v1/emails \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "x-api-key: pgn_your_key_here" \
  -d '{
    "to": "recipient@example.com",
    "subject": "Hello from Pigeons",
    "html": "<h1>It works!</h1>"
  }'
```

Response:

```json
{
  "id": "msg_abc123...",
  "status": "queued",
  "from": "noreply@yourdomain.com",
  "to": ["recipient@example.com"],
  "subject": "Hello from Pigeons"
}
```

## Install the SDK

### TypeScript

```bash
npm install @pigeons/pigeons-ts
```

```typescript
import { Pigeons } from '@pigeons/pigeons-ts'

const pigeons = new Pigeons({
  baseUrl: 'http://localhost:3891',
  apiKey: 'pgn_your_key_here',
})

const email = await pigeons.emails.send({
  to: 'recipient@example.com',
  subject: 'Hello from Pigeons',
  html: '<h1>It works!</h1>',
})

console.log(email.id) // msg_abc123...
```

### Python

```bash
pip install pigeons-py
```

```python
from pigeons import Pigeons

pigeons = Pigeons(
    base_url="http://localhost:3891",
    api_key="pgn_your_key_here",
)

email = pigeons.emails.send(
    to="recipient@example.com",
    subject="Hello from Pigeons",
    html="<h1>It works!</h1>",
)

print(email.id)  # msg_abc123...
```

## What's next

- [Self-Hosting](/docs/self-hosting) - production deployment with Docker, environment variables, and HTTPS
- [Domains](/docs/domains) - add and verify a sending domain
- [API Reference](/docs/api-reference) - full endpoint documentation
- [TypeScript SDK](/docs/typescript-sdk) - complete SDK guide


============================================================
Self-Hosting (self-hosting)
============================================================

---
title: Self-Hosting
description: Deploy Pigeons with Docker, configure AWS SES, and harden for production.
---

## Docker

```bash
docker run -d \
  --name pigeons \
  -p 3891:3891 \
  -v pigeons-data:/data \
  -e PIGEONS_DATABASE_URL=file:/data/pigeons.db \
  -e PIGEONS_AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=AKIA... \
  -e PIGEONS_AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=... \
  -e PIGEONS_AWS_REGION=us-east-1 \
  -e PIGEONS_FROM_EMAIL=noreply@yourdomain.com \
  -e PIGEONS_CONFIGURATION_SET=pigeons-tracking \
  ghcr.io/pigeons-dev/pigeons
```

On first start, Pigeons runs migrations, creates a default API key, and prints it to stdout. The key starts with `pgn_` and won't be shown again.

### Docker Compose

```yaml
services:
  pigeons:
    image: ghcr.io/pigeons-dev/pigeons
    ports:
      - "3891:3891"
    volumes:
      - pigeons-data:/data
    environment:
      PIGEONS_DATABASE_URL: file:/data/pigeons.db
      PIGEONS_AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID: ${AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID}
      PIGEONS_AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY: ${AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY}
      PIGEONS_AWS_REGION: us-east-1
      PIGEONS_FROM_EMAIL: noreply@yourdomain.com
      PIGEONS_CONFIGURATION_SET: pigeons-tracking
    restart: unless-stopped

volumes:
  pigeons-data:
```

## Environment Variables

| Variable | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `PIGEONS_PORT` | No | `3891` | HTTP server port |
| `PIGEONS_DATABASE_URL` | No | in-memory | SQLite database URL. Use `file:/path/to/pigeons.db` for persistence |
| `PIGEONS_AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID` | Yes | | AWS access key for SES |
| `PIGEONS_AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` | Yes | | AWS secret key for SES |
| `PIGEONS_AWS_REGION` | Yes | | AWS region (e.g. `us-east-1`) |
| `PIGEONS_FROM_EMAIL` | Yes | | Default sender email address |
| `PIGEONS_API_KEY` | No | auto-generated | Pre-set API key instead of auto-generating |
| `PIGEONS_WEBHOOK_SECRET` | No | | Default webhook signing secret |
| `PIGEONS_CONFIGURATION_SET` | No | | SES configuration set name for event tracking |
| `PIGEONS_WORKER_POLL_INTERVAL` | No | `1000` | Job queue poll interval in milliseconds |
| `PIGEONS_INBOUND_S3_BUCKET` | No | | S3 bucket for inbound email storage |
| `PIGEONS_INBOUND_S3_KEY_PREFIX` | No | | S3 key prefix for inbound emails (e.g. `inbound/`) |
| `PIGEONS_OPEN_TRACKING` | No | `false` | Enable open tracking globally |
| `PIGEONS_BASE_URL` | No | | Public base URL of this server (required for open tracking) |

## AWS SES Setup

Pigeons requires AWS SES for sending (and optionally receiving) email. You need:

1. An AWS account with SES access
2. IAM credentials with `ses:SendEmail`, `ses:SendRawEmail` permissions
3. A verified domain in SES
4. A configuration set for delivery event tracking

### Automated setup

The CLI wizard provisions all AWS resources in one command:

```bash
npx @pigeons/cli setup aws
```

It creates the SES domain identity, configuration set, SNS topics, S3 bucket (for inbound), and receipt rules. At the end it prints the DNS records to add and the environment variables to set.

Options:

```bash
npx @pigeons/cli setup aws \
  --region us-east-1 \
  --domain yourdomain.com \
  --access-key-id AKIA... \
  --secret-access-key ... \
  --skip-inbound  # skip inbound email setup
```

### Manual setup

If you prefer manual setup:

1. **Create SES domain identity** - verify your domain in the SES console
2. **Add DNS records** - DKIM CNAMEs, SPF TXT, DMARC TXT (see [Domains](/docs/domains))
3. **Create configuration set** - named `pigeons-tracking` (or any name, set via `PIGEONS_CONFIGURATION_SET`)
4. **Create SNS topic** for delivery events - subscribe it to `POST https://your-server/v1/internal/ses/events`
5. **Add SNS event destination** to the configuration set, matching events: `SEND`, `DELIVERY`, `BOUNCE`, `COMPLAINT`
6. **(Inbound only)** Create S3 bucket, SNS topic, and SES receipt rule (see [Inboxes](/docs/inboxes))

### SES Sandbox

New SES accounts start in sandbox mode. In sandbox:

- You can only send to verified email addresses
- You can send to SES simulator addresses: `success@simulator.amazonses.com`, `bounce@simulator.amazonses.com`, `complaint@simulator.amazonses.com`

Request production access through the AWS console when you're ready to send to any address.

## Production Checklist

### HTTPS

Pigeons itself serves HTTP. Put it behind a reverse proxy (nginx, Caddy, Traefik) for TLS:

```nginx
server {
    listen 443 ssl;
    server_name pigeons.yourdomain.com;

    ssl_certificate /path/to/cert.pem;
    ssl_certificate_key /path/to/key.pem;

    location / {
        proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:3891;
        proxy_set_header Host $host;
        proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $proxy_remote_addr;
        proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme;
    }
}
```

Set `PIGEONS_BASE_URL=https://pigeons.yourdomain.com` so open tracking pixels and links resolve correctly.

### Persistent storage

Always mount a volume for the database. Without it, data is lost when the container restarts:

```bash
-v pigeons-data:/data
-e PIGEONS_DATABASE_URL=file:/data/pigeons.db
```

### Monitoring

- `GET /health` returns `{ "status": "ok", "version": "0.1.0" }` - use this for health checks
- Watch Docker logs for job queue errors and delivery failures
- Set up a webhook for `email.bounced` and `email.complained` events to monitor deliverability

### SNS subscription

After starting the server, subscribe your SNS topics to the Pigeons endpoints:

```bash
# Delivery events (bounces, complaints, deliveries)
aws sns subscribe \
  --topic-arn arn:aws:sns:us-east-1:123456789:pigeons-events-yourdomain \
  --protocol https \
  --endpoint https://pigeons.yourdomain.com/v1/internal/ses/events

# Inbound email notifications
aws sns subscribe \
  --topic-arn arn:aws:sns:us-east-1:123456789:pigeons-inbound-yourdomain \
  --protocol https \
  --endpoint https://pigeons.yourdomain.com/v1/internal/ses/inbound
```

SNS will send a confirmation request to these endpoints. Pigeons handles confirmation automatically.


============================================================
API Reference (api-reference)
============================================================

---
title: API Reference
description: Complete REST API documentation for every Pigeons endpoint.
---

## Overview

Base path: `/v1`

All authenticated endpoints require the `x-api-key` header. API keys start with `pgn_`.

```bash
curl http://localhost:3891/v1/emails \
  -H "x-api-key: pgn_your_key_here"
```

### Pagination

List endpoints use cursor-based pagination:

```json
{
  "data": [...],
  "has_more": true,
  "next_cursor": "2024-01-15T10:30:00.000Z"
}
```

Pass `?cursor=<next_cursor>&limit=25` to get the next page. Maximum limit is 100, default is 25.

### Idempotency

Mutating endpoints accept an `Idempotency-Key` header. If the same key is sent again within 24 hours, the original response is returned without re-executing the request.

```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:3891/v1/emails \
  -H "x-api-key: pgn_..." \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: my-unique-key-123" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"to": "user@example.com", "subject": "Hello", "text": "Hi"}'
```

### Error format

All errors return a consistent JSON shape:

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "validation_error",
    "message": "Subject is required",
    "code": "validation_error"
  }
}
```

| Status | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| 400 | `validation_error` | Invalid request body or parameters |
| 401 | `authentication_error` | Missing or invalid API key |
| 404 | `not_found` | Resource does not exist |
| 409 | `conflict` | Resource already exists (e.g. duplicate email) |
| 429 | `rate_limit_error` | Too many requests |
| 500 | `internal_error` | Unexpected server error |

---

## Emails

### Send an email

```
POST /v1/emails
```

Send directly with HTML/text, or render a template by slug or ID.

**Request body:**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `to` | `string \| string[]` | Yes | Recipient address(es) |
| `from` | `string` | No | Sender address (defaults to `PIGEONS_FROM_EMAIL`) |
| `subject` | `string` | Conditional | Required unless using a template |
| `html` | `string` | Conditional | HTML body (required if no `text` or `templateId`) |
| `text` | `string` | Conditional | Plain text body |
| `templateId` | `string` | No | Template ID (`tpl_...`) or slug |
| `data` | `object` | No | Template variables |
| `cc` | `string[]` | No | CC recipients |
| `bcc` | `string[]` | No | BCC recipients |
| `tags` | `string[]` | No | Tags for filtering |
| `headers` | `object` | No | Custom email headers |
| `scheduledAt` | `string` | No | ISO 8601 timestamp for scheduled send |
| `trackOpens` | `boolean` | No | Override global open tracking for this email |

**Response (201):**

```json
{
  "id": "msg_abc123...",
  "status": "queued",
  "from": "noreply@yourdomain.com",
  "to": ["recipient@example.com"],
  "subject": "Hello"
}
```

### Get an email

```
GET /v1/emails/:id
```

Returns the full email object including delivery status, open tracking data, and timestamps.

**Response (200):**

```json
{
  "id": "msg_abc123...",
  "from": "noreply@yourdomain.com",
  "to": ["recipient@example.com"],
  "subject": "Hello",
  "html": "<h1>Hello</h1>",
  "status": "delivered",
  "sesMessageId": "...",
  "trackOpens": false,
  "openCount": 0,
  "firstOpenedAt": null,
  "lastOpenedAt": null,
  "tags": null,
  "scheduledAt": null,
  "createdAt": "2024-01-15T10:30:00.000Z",
  "updatedAt": "2024-01-15T10:30:05.000Z"
}
```

### List emails

```
GET /v1/emails
```

**Query parameters:**

| Param | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `limit` | `number` | Max results (default 25, max 100) |
| `cursor` | `string` | Pagination cursor |
| `status` | `string` | Filter by status: `queued`, `sending`, `sent`, `delivered`, `bounced`, `complained`, `failed` |

### Cancel a queued email

```
POST /v1/emails/:id/cancel
```

Only emails with status `queued` can be cancelled. Sets status to `failed`.

### Batch send

```
POST /v1/emails/batch
```

Send up to 100 emails in a single request. Request body is an array of send email objects.

**Response (201):** Array of email objects, one per item.

---

## Domains

### Add a domain

```
POST /v1/domains
```

**Request body:**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `domain` | `string` | Yes | Domain name (e.g. `example.com`) |
| `capabilities` | `object` | No | `{ sending: true, receiving: false }` |

**Response (201):** Domain object with DKIM tokens and required DNS records.

### List domains

```
GET /v1/domains
```

**Response (200):**

```json
{
  "data": [
    {
      "id": "dom_abc123...",
      "domain": "example.com",
      "verificationStatus": "verified",
      "dkimTokens": ["token1", "token2", "token3"],
      "spfVerified": true,
      "dmarcVerified": true,
      "region": "us-east-1",
      "capabilities": { "sending": true, "receiving": false },
      "records": [...]
    }
  ]
}
```

### Get domain

```
GET /v1/domains/:id
```

### Verify a domain

```
GET /v1/domains/:id/verify
```

Re-checks DNS records and updates verification status.

### Get domain stats

```
GET /v1/domains/:id/stats
```

Returns delivery statistics and warmup guidance for the domain.

### Delete a domain

```
DELETE /v1/domains/:id
```

---

## Contacts

### Create a contact

```
POST /v1/contacts
```

**Request body:**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `email` | `string` | Yes | Email address (must be unique) |
| `firstName` | `string` | No | First name |
| `lastName` | `string` | No | Last name |
| `tags` | `string[]` | No | Tags for segmentation |
| `properties` | `object` | No | Custom key-value data |

**Response (201):** Full contact object.

### Get a contact

```
GET /v1/contacts/:idOrEmail
```

Accepts either a contact ID (`ctc_...`) or email address.

### List contacts

```
GET /v1/contacts
```

**Query parameters:**

| Param | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `limit` | `number` | Max results (default 25, max 100) |
| `cursor` | `string` | Pagination cursor |
| `tag` | `string` | Filter by tag |

### Update a contact

```
PATCH /v1/contacts/:idOrEmail
```

**Request body:**

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `firstName` | `string` | First name |
| `lastName` | `string` | Last name |
| `tags` | `string[]` | Replace tags |
| `properties` | `object` | Replace custom properties |

### Delete a contact

```
DELETE /v1/contacts/:idOrEmail
```

### Batch create contacts

```
POST /v1/contacts/batch
```

Create up to 1000 contacts. Existing emails are silently skipped.

**Request body:** Array of contact creation objects.

**Response (201):**

```json
{
  "created": 8,
  "skipped": 2,
  "contacts": [{ "id": "ctc_...", "email": "..." }, ...]
}
```

### Unsubscribe a contact

```
POST /v1/contacts/:idOrEmail/unsubscribe
```

Global unsubscribe, or pass `{ "topicId": "top_..." }` for per-topic unsubscribe.

### Resubscribe a contact

```
POST /v1/contacts/:idOrEmail/resubscribe
```

Same body format as unsubscribe.

---

## Templates

### Create a template

```
POST /v1/templates
```

**Request body:**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `slug` | `string` | Yes | URL-safe identifier (lowercase alphanumeric with hyphens) |
| `name` | `string` | Yes | Display name |
| `subject` | `string` | Yes | Subject line (supports `{{variables}}`) |
| `body` | `string` | Yes | HTML body (supports `{{variables}}`) |
| `sampleData` | `object` | No | Sample data for previews |

### Get a template

```
GET /v1/templates/:idOrSlug
```

Accepts template ID (`tpl_...`) or slug.

### List templates

```
GET /v1/templates
```

### Update a template

```
PATCH /v1/templates/:idOrSlug
```

Updating `body` or `subject` increments the template version.

### Delete a template

```
DELETE /v1/templates/:idOrSlug
```

### Preview a template

```
POST /v1/templates/:idOrSlug/preview
```

**Request body:**

```json
{ "data": { "name": "Alice", "company": "Acme" } }
```

**Response (200):**

```json
{
  "subject": "Welcome, Alice!",
  "html": "<h1>Welcome to Acme</h1>...",
  "text": "Welcome to Acme..."
}
```

---

## Campaigns

### Create a campaign

```
POST /v1/campaigns
```

Creates a campaign in `draft` status.

**Request body:**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | `string` | Yes | Campaign name |
| `subject` | `string` | No | Email subject (or use template) |
| `topicId` | `string` | No | Subscription topic ID for unsubscribe filtering |
| `templateId` | `string` | No | Template ID or slug |
| `templateData` | `object` | No | Template variables |
| `fromName` | `string` | No | Sender display name |
| `fromEmail` | `string` | No | Sender email address |
| `audienceFilter` | `object` | No | Filter to select recipients (see [Audience Filters](#audience-filters)) |
| `scheduledAt` | `string` | No | ISO 8601 timestamp for scheduled send |

### List campaigns

```
GET /v1/campaigns
```

**Query parameters:** `limit`, `cursor`, `status` (`draft`, `scheduled`, `sending`, `paused`, `sent`, `cancelled`).

### Get a campaign

```
GET /v1/campaigns/:id
```

Returns the campaign with its `stats` object:

```json
{
  "stats": {
    "total": 500,
    "sent": 450,
    "delivered": 440,
    "opened": 120,
    "bounced": 5,
    "complained": 1,
    "failed": 4
  }
}
```

### Update a campaign

```
PATCH /v1/campaigns/:id
```

Only `draft` campaigns can be updated.

### Send a campaign

```
POST /v1/campaigns/:id/send
```

Transitions from `draft` or `scheduled` to `sending`. Filters contacts by audience filter, excluding unsubscribed, bounced, and complained contacts.

Optional body: `{ "scheduledAt": "2024-06-01T09:00:00Z" }` to schedule instead of sending immediately.

### Pause a campaign

```
POST /v1/campaigns/:id/pause
```

Only `sending` campaigns can be paused.

### Resume a campaign

```
POST /v1/campaigns/:id/resume
```

Only `paused` campaigns can be resumed.

### Cancel a campaign

```
POST /v1/campaigns/:id/cancel
```

Only `sending` or `scheduled` campaigns can be cancelled.

### Audience Filters

The `audienceFilter` object supports:

```json
{
  "tags": {
    "contains": "newsletter",
    "containsAny": ["vip", "early-adopter"],
    "containsAll": ["active", "verified"]
  },
  "properties": {
    "plan": "pro",
    "region": "us"
  }
}
```

---

## Sequences

### Create a sequence

```
POST /v1/sequences
```

**Request body:**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | `string` | Yes | Sequence name |
| `trigger` | `object` | No | `{ event: "contact.created", filter: {...} }` |
| `steps` | `array` | No | Array of step objects |

**Step types:**

- `email` - send an email using `templateId` and optional `subject`, `templateData`, `topicId`
- `delay` - wait for a duration (e.g. `"1d"`, `"12h"`, `"30m"`) via `delayDuration`
- `condition` - evaluate a condition before continuing

### List sequences

```
GET /v1/sequences
```

**Query parameters:** `limit`, `cursor`, `status` (`draft`, `active`, `paused`, `archived`).

### Get a sequence

```
GET /v1/sequences/:id
```

Returns the sequence with all steps and stats.

### Update a sequence

```
PATCH /v1/sequences/:id
```

Active sequences must be paused before updating. Steps are replaced wholesale when provided.

### Activate a sequence

```
POST /v1/sequences/:id/activate
```

Sequence must have at least one step.

### Pause a sequence

```
POST /v1/sequences/:id/pause
```

### Enroll a contact

```
POST /v1/sequences/:id/enroll
```

**Request body:**

```json
{ "contactId": "ctc_abc123..." }
```

Sequence must be `active`. Returns the enrollment object.

### List enrollments

```
GET /v1/sequences/:id/enrollments
```

**Query parameters:** `limit`, `cursor`, `status` (`active`, `completed`, `exited`, `failed`).

---

## Inboxes

### Create an inbox

```
POST /v1/inboxes
```

**Request body:**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | `string` | Yes | Inbox name |
| `emailAddress` | `string` | Yes | Email address for this inbox |
| `description` | `string` | No | Description |
| `webhookUrl` | `string` | No | URL to receive inbound message webhooks |
| `metadata` | `object` | No | Arbitrary metadata |
| `labels` | `string[]` | No | Labels for categorization |

### List inboxes

```
GET /v1/inboxes
```

**Query parameters:** `limit`, `cursor`, `status` (`active`, `paused`, `archived`), `label`.

### Get an inbox

```
GET /v1/inboxes/:id
```

### Update an inbox

```
PATCH /v1/inboxes/:id
```

### Delete an inbox

```
DELETE /v1/inboxes/:id
```

### Pause an inbox

```
POST /v1/inboxes/:id/pause
```

### Resume an inbox

```
POST /v1/inboxes/:id/resume
```

### Set catch-all

```
POST /v1/inboxes/:id/catch-all
```

Designates this inbox as the catch-all for unmatched inbound emails. Only one inbox can be catch-all at a time.

### List messages

```
GET /v1/inboxes/:id/messages
```

**Query parameters:** `limit`, `cursor`, `direction` (`inbound`, `outbound`), `thread_id`, `label`.

### Get a message

```
GET /v1/inboxes/:id/messages/:messageId
```

### Send a message

```
POST /v1/inboxes/:id/messages
```

**Request body:**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `to` | `string \| string[]` | Yes | Recipient address(es) |
| `cc` | `string[]` | No | CC recipients |
| `subject` | `string` | No | Subject line |
| `html` | `string` | Conditional | HTML body |
| `text` | `string` | Conditional | Plain text body |
| `inReplyTo` | `string` | No | Message ID to reply to (maintains threading) |
| `labels` | `string[]` | No | Labels |

### List threads

```
GET /v1/inboxes/:id/threads
```

**Query parameters:** `limit`, `cursor`, `status` (`open`, `closed`, `snoozed`).

### Get a thread

```
GET /v1/inboxes/:id/threads/:threadId
```

### Update a thread

```
PATCH /v1/inboxes/:id/threads/:threadId
```

**Request body:**

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `status` | `string` | `open`, `closed`, or `snoozed` |
| `metadata` | `object` | Arbitrary metadata |

---

## Webhooks

### Create a webhook

```
POST /v1/webhooks
```

**Request body:**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `url` | `string` | Yes | Endpoint URL |
| `events` | `string[]` | Yes | Event types to subscribe to |
| `secret` | `string` | No | Signing secret (min 16 chars). Auto-generated if omitted |

The response includes the `secret` field. It is not returned on subsequent GET requests.

### List webhooks

```
GET /v1/webhooks
```

### Get a webhook

```
GET /v1/webhooks/:id
```

### Update a webhook

```
PATCH /v1/webhooks/:id
```

**Request body:**

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `url` | `string` | New endpoint URL |
| `events` | `string[]` | New event list |
| `status` | `string` | `active` or `disabled` |

### Delete a webhook

```
DELETE /v1/webhooks/:id
```

---

## API Keys

### Create an API key

```
POST /v1/api-keys
```

**Request body:**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | `string` | Yes | Key name for identification |
| `scopes` | `string[]` | No | Restrict to specific scopes (omit for full access) |
| `expiresAt` | `string` | No | ISO 8601 expiration timestamp |

Available scopes: `emails`, `domains`, `api_keys`, `templates`, `contacts`, `inboxes`, `webhooks`, `campaigns`, `sequences`, `topics`, `stats`, or `*` for all.

**Response (201):** Includes the full API key in the `key` field. This is the only time the key is returned.

### List API keys

```
GET /v1/api-keys
```

Returns all keys with `prefix` (first characters) but not the full key.

### Delete an API key

```
DELETE /v1/api-keys/:id
```

---

## Unauthenticated Endpoints

These endpoints sit outside auth middleware:

| Method | Path | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `GET` | `/health` | Health check - returns `{ "status": "ok" }` |
| `POST` | `/v1/internal/ses/events` | SES delivery/bounce/complaint events via SNS |
| `POST` | `/v1/internal/ses/inbound` | SES inbound email notifications via SNS |
| `GET` | `/v1/t/:emailId` | Open tracking pixel (1x1 transparent GIF) |

TypeScript SDK (typescript-sdk)
============================================================

---
title: TypeScript SDK
description: Send emails, manage contacts, and build automations with the TypeScript SDK.
---

## Install

```bash
npm install @pigeons/pigeons-ts
```

## Initialize

```typescript
import { Pigeons } from '@pigeons/pigeons-ts'

const pigeons = new Pigeons({
  baseUrl: 'https://pigeons.yourdomain.com',
  apiKey: 'pgn_your_key_here',
})
```

Both options can be set via environment variables instead:

| Option | Env var | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `baseUrl` | `PIGEONS_URL` | Pigeons server URL (no default) |
| `apiKey` | `PIGEONS_API_KEY` | API key starting with `pgn_` |

Constructor values take precedence over environment variables.

---

## Emails

### Send an email

```typescript
const email = await pigeons.emails.send({
  to: 'alice@example.com',
  subject: 'Welcome!',
  html: '<h1>Welcome aboard</h1>',
})

console.log(email.id)     // msg_abc123...
console.log(email.status) // "queued"
```

### Send with a template

```typescript
const email = await pigeons.emails.send({
  to: 'alice@example.com',
  templateId: 'welcome-email', // slug or tpl_ ID
  data: { name: 'Alice', company: 'Acme' },
})
```

### Multiple recipients

```typescript
const email = await pigeons.emails.send({
  to: ['alice@example.com', 'bob@example.com'],
  cc: ['manager@example.com'],
  subject: 'Team Update',
  html: '<p>Here is your update.</p>',
})
```

### Schedule an email

```typescript
const email = await pigeons.emails.send({
  to: 'alice@example.com',
  subject: 'Reminder',
  text: 'Your trial expires tomorrow.',
  scheduledAt: '2024-06-01T09:00:00Z',
})
```

### Get email status

```typescript
const email = await pigeons.emails.get('msg_abc123...')
console.log(email.status) // "delivered"
```

### List emails

```typescript
const page = await pigeons.emails.list({ limit: 10, status: 'delivered' })

for (const email of page.data) {
  console.log(email.id, email.subject, email.status)
}

if (page.has_more) {
  const next = await pigeons.emails.list({ cursor: page.next_cursor! })
}
```

### Cancel a queued email

```typescript
const cancelled = await pigeons.emails.cancel('msg_abc123...')
```

### Batch send

```typescript
const results = await pigeons.emails.batch([
  { to: 'alice@example.com', subject: 'Hi Alice', text: 'Hello!' },
  { to: 'bob@example.com', subject: 'Hi Bob', text: 'Hello!' },
])
```

### Idempotent sends

```typescript
const email = await pigeons.emails.send(
  { to: 'alice@example.com', subject: 'Order #123', html: '...' },
  { idempotencyKey: 'order-123-confirmation' },
)
```

## Contacts

### Create a contact

```typescript
const contact = await pigeons.contacts.create({
  email: 'alice@example.com',
  firstName: 'Alice',
  lastName: 'Smith',
  tags: ['newsletter', 'beta'],
  properties: { plan: 'pro', signupSource: 'website' },
})
```

### Get a contact

```typescript
// By ID
const contact = await pigeons.contacts.get('ctc_abc123...')

// By email
const contact = await pigeons.contacts.get('alice@example.com')
```

### Update a contact

```typescript
const updated = await pigeons.contacts.update('ctc_abc123...', {
  tags: ['newsletter', 'beta', 'vip'],
  properties: { plan: 'enterprise' },
})
```

### List contacts

```typescript
const page = await pigeons.contacts.list({ tag: 'newsletter', limit: 50 })
```

### Delete a contact

```typescript
await pigeons.contacts.delete('ctc_abc123...')
```

### Batch create

```typescript
const result = await pigeons.contacts.batchCreate([
  { email: 'alice@example.com', firstName: 'Alice', tags: ['import'] },
  { email: 'bob@example.com', firstName: 'Bob', tags: ['import'] },
])
console.log(result.created) // 2
console.log(result.skipped) // 0
```

### Unsubscribe / Resubscribe

```typescript
// Global unsubscribe
await pigeons.contacts.unsubscribe('ctc_abc123...')

// Per-topic unsubscribe
await pigeons.contacts.unsubscribe('ctc_abc123...', { topicId: 'top_xyz...' })

// Resubscribe
await pigeons.contacts.resubscribe('ctc_abc123...')
```

## Templates

### Create a template

```typescript
const template = await pigeons.templates.create({
  slug: 'welcome-email',
  name: 'Welcome Email',
  subject: 'Welcome, {{name}}!',
  body: '<h1>Welcome to {{company}}</h1><p>Hi {{name}},</p>',
  sampleData: { name: 'Alice', company: 'Acme' },
})
```

### Get / Update / Delete

```typescript
const tpl = await pigeons.templates.get('welcome-email') // by slug or ID
const updated = await pigeons.templates.update('welcome-email', { subject: 'New subject' })
await pigeons.templates.delete('welcome-email')
```

### Preview a template

```typescript
const preview = await pigeons.templates.preview('welcome-email', {
  name: 'Alice',
  company: 'Acme',
})
console.log(preview.subject) // "Welcome, Alice!"
console.log(preview.html)    // rendered HTML
```

## Campaigns

### Create and send a campaign

```typescript
const campaign = await pigeons.campaigns.create({
  name: 'Product Launch',
  templateId: 'product-launch',
  templateData: { launchDate: '2024-06-01' },
  audienceFilter: { tags: { contains: 'newsletter' } },
})

// Send immediately
await pigeons.campaigns.send(campaign.id)

// Or schedule
await pigeons.campaigns.send(campaign.id, {
  scheduledAt: '2024-06-01T09:00:00Z',
})
```

### Campaign lifecycle

```typescript
await pigeons.campaigns.pause(campaign.id)
await pigeons.campaigns.resume(campaign.id)
await pigeons.campaigns.cancel(campaign.id)
```

### Monitor stats

```typescript
const campaign = await pigeons.campaigns.get('cmp_abc123...')
console.log(campaign.stats)
// { total: 500, sent: 450, delivered: 440, opened: 120, bounced: 5, complained: 1, failed: 4 }
```

## Sequences

### Create a sequence

```typescript
const sequence = await pigeons.sequences.create({
  name: 'Onboarding',
  steps: [
    { type: 'email', templateId: 'welcome-email', subject: 'Welcome!' },
    { type: 'delay', delayDuration: '1d' },
    { type: 'email', templateId: 'getting-started', subject: 'Getting Started' },
    { type: 'delay', delayDuration: '3d' },
    { type: 'email', templateId: 'tips', subject: 'Pro Tips' },
  ],
})
```

### Activate and enroll

```typescript
await pigeons.sequences.activate(sequence.id)

const enrollment = await pigeons.sequences.enroll(sequence.id, 'ctc_abc123...')
console.log(enrollment.status) // "active"
```

### Monitor enrollments

```typescript
const page = await pigeons.sequences.enrollments(sequence.id, { status: 'active' })
```

## Inboxes

### Create an inbox

```typescript
const inbox = await pigeons.inboxes.create({
  name: 'Support',
  emailAddress: 'support@yourdomain.com',
  webhookUrl: 'https://your-app.com/webhooks/email',
})
```

### Inbox operations

```typescript
await pigeons.inboxes.pause(inbox.id)
await pigeons.inboxes.resume(inbox.id)
await pigeons.inboxes.setCatchAll(inbox.id)
await pigeons.inboxes.delete(inbox.id)
```

### Read messages

```typescript
const messages = await pigeons.inboxes.messages.list(inbox.id, {
  direction: 'inbound',
  limit: 10,
})

const message = await pigeons.inboxes.messages.get(inbox.id, 'imsg_abc123...')
```

### Send from an inbox

```typescript
const sent = await pigeons.inboxes.messages.create(inbox.id, {
  to: 'customer@example.com',
  subject: 'Re: Your ticket',
  html: '<p>Thanks for reaching out.</p>',
  inReplyTo: 'imsg_previous...', // maintains thread
})
```

### Threads

```typescript
const threads = await pigeons.inboxes.threads.list(inbox.id, { status: 'open' })

const thread = await pigeons.inboxes.threads.get(inbox.id, 'thr_abc123...')

await pigeons.inboxes.threads.update(inbox.id, 'thr_abc123...', {
  status: 'closed',
})
```

## Webhooks

```typescript
const webhook = await pigeons.webhooks.create({
  url: 'https://your-app.com/webhooks/pigeons',
  events: ['email.delivered', 'email.bounced', 'inbox.message.received'],
})

// The secret is only returned on creation
console.log(webhook.secret) // "whsec_..."
```

## Domains

```typescript
const domain = await pigeons.domains.add({ domain: 'example.com' })
console.log(domain.records) // DNS records to add

// Re-check verification
const verified = await pigeons.domains.verify(domain.id)
console.log(verified.verificationStatus) // "verified"
```

---

## Error Handling

All errors extend `PigeonsError`:

```typescript
import { PigeonsError, NotFoundError, AuthError, RateLimitError } from '@pigeons/pigeons-ts'

try {
  await pigeons.emails.get('msg_nonexistent')
} catch (err) {
  if (err instanceof NotFoundError) {
    console.log(err.message)    // "Email 'msg_nonexistent' not found"
    console.log(err.statusCode) // 404
    console.log(err.code)       // "not_found"
    console.log(err.type)       // "not_found"
  }
}
```

Error classes:

| Class | Status | When |
|---|---|---|
| `PigeonsError` | varies | Base class for all errors |
| `ValidationError` | 400 | Invalid request parameters |
| `AuthError` | 401 | Missing or invalid API key |
| `NotFoundError` | 404 | Resource not found |
| `RateLimitError` | 429 | Rate limit exceeded |
