## Error Handling

All errors extend `PigeonsError`:

```python
from pigeons import PigeonsError, NotFoundError, AuthError, RateLimitError

try:
    pigeons.emails.get("msg_nonexistent")
except NotFoundError as e:
    print(e.message)      # "Email 'msg_nonexistent' not found"
    print(e.status_code)  # 404
    print(e.code)         # "not_found"
except PigeonsError as e:
    print(f"API error: {e.message}")
```

Error classes:

| Class | Status | When |
|---|---|---|
| `PigeonsError` | varies | Base class for all errors |
| `ValidationError` | 400 | Invalid request parameters |
| `AuthError` | 401 | Missing or invalid API key |
| `NotFoundError` | 404 | Resource not found |
| `RateLimitError` | 429 | Rate limit exceeded |


============================================================
CLI (cli)
============================================================

---
title: CLI
description: Manage your Pigeons instance from the command line.
---

## Install

```bash
# Run directly
npx @pigeons/cli <command>

# Or install globally
npm install -g @pigeons/cli
pigeons <command>
```

## Configuration

The CLI resolves credentials in this order:

1. **Flags** - `--url` and `--api-key` passed to the command
2. **Environment variables** - `PIGEONS_URL` and `PIGEONS_API_KEY`
3. **Config file** - `~/.config/pigeons/config.json`

### Login

Store your server URL and API key in the config file:

```bash
pigeons login --url https://pigeons.yourdomain.com
```

You'll be prompted for your API key. Credentials are saved to `~/.config/pigeons/config.json`.

### Check connection

```bash
pigeons whoami
```

Verifies the API key is valid and prints the key name and scopes.

### Status

```bash
pigeons status
```

Shows server health, domain verification status, and recent email activity.

---

## Commands

### send

Send a single email:

```bash
pigeons send \
  --to alice@example.com \
  --subject "Hello from Pigeons" \
  --html "<h1>Hello!</h1>"
```

Options:

| Flag | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--to <email>` | Yes | Recipient address |
| `--subject <text>` | Yes | Subject line |
| `--from <email>` | No | Sender address (uses server default) |
| `--html <html>` | Conditional | HTML body (required if no `--text`) |
| `--text <text>` | Conditional | Plain text body (required if no `--html`) |

### emails

```bash
pigeons emails list              # list recent emails
pigeons emails get <id>          # get email details
```

### domains

```bash
pigeons domains add <domain>     # add a new domain
pigeons domains list             # list all domains
pigeons domains verify <id>      # re-check DNS verification
```

When you add a domain, Pigeons registers it with SES and returns the DNS records you need to add. Run `verify` after adding the records to confirm verification.

### contacts

```bash
pigeons contacts list            # list contacts
pigeons contacts list --tag vip  # filter by tag
```

### templates

```bash
pigeons templates list           # list all templates
```

### campaigns

```bash
pigeons campaigns list           # list campaigns
pigeons campaigns list --status draft  # filter by status
```

### sequences

```bash
pigeons sequences list           # list sequences
```

### webhooks

```bash
pigeons webhooks list            # list webhooks
```

### topics

```bash
pigeons topics list              # list subscription topics
```

### inboxes

```bash
pigeons inboxes list             # list inboxes
```

### setup aws

Provision all AWS resources needed for a Pigeons instance:

```bash
pigeons setup aws
```

The wizard interactively collects your AWS credentials, region, and domain, then creates:

- SES domain identity with DKIM
- SES configuration set (`pigeons-tracking`)
- SNS topic for delivery events
- S3 bucket for inbound emails (unless `--skip-inbound`)
- SNS topic for inbound notifications
- SES receipt rule set and rule

At the end it prints:
- DNS records to add (DKIM CNAMEs, SPF, MX, DMARC)
- Environment variables to set
- SNS topic ARNs to subscribe to your server

Options:

```bash
pigeons setup aws \
  --region us-east-1 \
  --domain yourdomain.com \
  --access-key-id AKIA... \
  --secret-access-key ... \
  --skip-inbound
```

SES inbound email is only available in `us-east-1`, `us-west-2`, and `eu-west-1`. If you choose another region, inbound setup is automatically skipped.

---

## Global Options

Every command accepts:

| Flag | Description |
|---|---|
| `--url <url>` | Override the Pigeons instance URL |
| `--api-key <key>` | Override the API key |


============================================================
MCP Server (mcp)
============================================================

---
title: MCP Server
description: Give LLM agents the ability to send emails, manage inboxes, and run campaigns.
---

## Overview

The Pigeons MCP (Model Context Protocol) server exposes Pigeons operations as tools that LLM agents can call. This lets Claude, GPT, and other agents send emails, manage contacts, read inboxes, and run campaigns through natural language.

## Install

```bash
npm install -g @pigeons/mcp
```

## Configure in Claude Desktop

Add to your `claude_desktop_config.json`:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "pigeons": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "@pigeons/mcp", "--url", "https://pigeons.yourdomain.com", "--api-key", "pgn_your_key_here"]
    }
  }
}
```

Or use environment variables:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "pigeons": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "@pigeons/mcp"],
      "env": {
        "PIGEONS_URL": "https://pigeons.yourdomain.com",
        "PIGEONS_API_KEY": "pgn_your_key_here"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

## Configure in Claude Code

Add to your project's `.claude/settings.json` or global settings:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "pigeons": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "@pigeons/mcp"],
      "env": {
        "PIGEONS_URL": "https://pigeons.yourdomain.com",
        "PIGEONS_API_KEY": "pgn_your_key_here"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

## Available Tools

### Email tools

| Tool | Description |
|---|---|
| `send_email` | Send a transactional email with HTML/text or a template |
| `get_email` | Get email details and delivery status by ID |
| `list_emails` | List sent emails with optional status filtering |

### Inbox tools

| Tool | Description |
|---|---|
| `create_inbox` | Create a new agent inbox with a real email address |
| `list_inboxes` | List all agent inboxes |
| `get_inbox_messages` | Get messages for an inbox, optionally filtered by thread or direction |
| `get_thread` | Get a full conversation thread |
| `reply_to_message` | Send a reply from an inbox, maintaining the conversation thread |
| `update_thread_status` | Update thread status (open, closed, snoozed) |

### Contact tools

| Tool | Description |
|---|---|
| `create_contact` | Create a new contact |
| `search_contacts` | List contacts with tag or email filtering |
| `update_contact` | Update a contact's properties, tags, or name |

### Template tools

| Tool | Description |
|---|---|
| `list_templates` | List available email templates |
| `preview_template` | Render a template with sample data |

### Campaign tools

| Tool | Description |
|---|---|
| `create_campaign` | Create a draft email campaign |
| `list_campaigns` | List campaigns with optional status filter |
| `get_campaign` | Get campaign details and statistics |
| `send_campaign` | Send or schedule a campaign |
| `cancel_campaign` | Cancel a sending or scheduled campaign |

### Sequence tools

| Tool | Description |
|---|---|
| `create_sequence` | Create a multi-step email sequence |
| `list_sequences` | List sequences |
| `get_sequence` | Get sequence details with steps and stats |
| `activate_sequence` | Activate a sequence |
| `pause_sequence` | Pause an active sequence |
| `enroll_in_sequence` | Enroll a contact in a sequence |

### Topic tools

| Tool | Description |
|---|---|
| `create_topic` | Create a subscription topic |
| `list_topics` | List subscription topics |
| `get_topic` | Get topic details |
| `delete_topic` | Delete a topic |

## Resources

The MCP server also exposes read-only resources:

| Resource URI | Description |
|---|---|
| `pigeons://inboxes` | All agent inboxes and their email addresses |
| `pigeons://templates` | Available templates with slugs and variable schemas |
| `pigeons://domains` | Verified sending domains and their status |

## Example Prompts

Once configured, you can ask your LLM agent:

- "Send a welcome email to alice@example.com using the welcome-email template"
- "Check the status of email msg_abc123"
- "Show me all undelivered emails from today"
- "Create an inbox for support@mycompany.com"
- "Read the latest messages in the support inbox"
- "Reply to the customer in thread thr_xyz saying we'll look into it"
- "Create a campaign called 'Product Launch' targeting contacts tagged with 'beta'"
- "What are the delivery stats for the Product Launch campaign?"
- "Create an onboarding sequence with a welcome email, 1-day delay, then a getting-started email"
- "Enroll contact ctc_abc123 in the onboarding sequence"


============================================================
Domains & DNS (domains)
============================================================

---
title: Domains
description: Add, verify, and configure sending domains.
---

## Add a Domain

Register a domain with Pigeons and SES:

```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:3891/v1/domains \
  -H "x-api-key: pgn_..." \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"domain": "yourdomain.com"}'
```

Or via the CLI:

```bash
pigeons domains add yourdomain.com
```

Pigeons calls `CreateEmailIdentity` on SES, which returns DKIM tokens. The response includes the full list of DNS records you need to add.

## DNS Records

After adding a domain, you need to configure these DNS records:

### DKIM (required)

Three CNAME records for email authentication. The exact values come from the domain response:

```
CNAME  token1._domainkey.yourdomain.com  →  token1.dkim.amazonses.com
CNAME  token2._domainkey.yourdomain.com  →  token2.dkim.amazonses.com
CNAME  token3._domainkey.yourdomain.com  →  token3.dkim.amazonses.com
```

### SPF (required)

A TXT record authorizing SES to send on your behalf:

```
TXT  mail.yourdomain.com  →  "v=spf1 include:amazonses.com ~all"
```

### DMARC (recommended)

A TXT record for DMARC policy. Start with `quarantine` and tighten to `reject` once deliverability is confirmed:

```
TXT  _dmarc.yourdomain.com  →  "v=DMARC1; p=quarantine; rua=mailto:dmarc@yourdomain.com"
```

### MX for outbound feedback

An MX record for bounce feedback:

```
MX  mail.yourdomain.com  →  10 feedback-smtp.us-east-1.amazonses.com
```

Replace `us-east-1` with your SES region.

### MX for inbound (optional)

If you want to receive email through Pigeons inboxes:

```
MX  yourdomain.com  →  10 inbound-smtp.us-east-1.amazonaws.com
```

Inbound MX is only available in `us-east-1`, `us-west-2`, and `eu-west-1`.

## Verification

After adding DNS records, trigger a verification check:

```bash
curl http://localhost:3891/v1/domains/dom_abc123.../verify \
  -H "x-api-key: pgn_..."
```

Or:

```bash
pigeons domains verify dom_abc123...
```

Pigeons queries SES for the identity's current verification state and updates the stored status. DNS propagation typically takes 5-10 minutes, but can take up to 72 hours.

The domain object tracks three verification fields:

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| `verificationStatus` | Overall status: `pending`, `verified`, or `failed` |
| `spfVerified` | Whether SPF record is detected |
| `dmarcVerified` | Whether DMARC record is detected |

## Domain Stats

Check sending metrics for a domain:

```bash
curl http://localhost:3891/v1/domains/dom_abc123.../stats \
  -H "x-api-key: pgn_..."
```

Returns delivery rates, bounce rates, and warmup guidance across three time windows (24h, 7d, 30d).

## Region Considerations

Each domain is associated with an AWS region. SES treats each region as a separate sending environment:

- Sending reputation is per-region
- Sandbox status is per-region
- Inbound email is only available in `us-east-1`, `us-west-2`, and `eu-west-1`
- DKIM tokens are region-specific

If you need to send from multiple regions, add the same domain in each region. DNS records may differ.

## SES Sandbox vs Production

New SES accounts start in **sandbox mode** per region. In sandbox:

- You can only send to verified email addresses
- Daily sending limit: 200 emails
- Maximum send rate: 1 email per second
- You can test with SES simulator addresses:
  - `success@simulator.amazonses.com` - simulates successful delivery
  - `bounce@simulator.amazonses.com` - simulates a hard bounce
  - `complaint@simulator.amazonses.com` - simulates a complaint

To move out of sandbox, request production access in the AWS console for your region. AWS reviews the request (typically 24 hours) and evaluates your sending use case.

## Capabilities

When adding a domain, you can specify capabilities:

```json
{
  "domain": "yourdomain.com",
  "capabilities": {
    "sending": true,
    "receiving": false
  }
}
```

- `sending: true` - domain can be used as a `from` address (default)
- `receiving: true` - domain accepts inbound email through Pigeons inboxes (requires MX record and SES receipt rule)

## Delete a Domain

```bash
curl -X DELETE http://localhost:3891/v1/domains/dom_abc123... \
  -H "x-api-key: pgn_..."
```

This removes the domain from Pigeons and deletes the SES identity. DNS records should be cleaned up manually.


============================================================
Contacts (contacts)
============================================================

---
title: Contacts
description: Manage contacts, tags, properties, and subscription preferences.
---

## Create a Contact

```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:3891/v1/contacts \
  -H "x-api-key: pgn_..." \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "email": "alice@example.com",
    "firstName": "Alice",
    "lastName": "Smith",
    "tags": ["newsletter", "beta"],
    "properties": {"plan": "pro", "company": "Acme"}
  }'
```

```typescript
const contact = await pigeons.contacts.create({
  email: 'alice@example.com',
  firstName: 'Alice',
  tags: ['newsletter', 'beta'],
  properties: { plan: 'pro', company: 'Acme' },
})
```

Email addresses must be unique. Creating a contact with an existing email returns a 409 conflict.

## Tags

Tags are freeform strings used for segmentation. Use them to categorize contacts and target campaigns.

```json
{
  "tags": ["newsletter", "beta", "enterprise"]
}
```

Tags are stored as an array on the contact. When updating tags, the entire array is replaced (not merged). To add a tag without removing existing ones, read the current tags first.

### Filter by tag

```bash
curl "http://localhost:3891/v1/contacts?tag=newsletter" \
  -H "x-api-key: pgn_..."
```

### Use tags in audience filters

Campaigns and sequences use tags to target recipients:

```json
{
  "audienceFilter": {
    "tags": {
      "contains": "newsletter"
    }
  }
}
```

Available tag filters:

| Filter | Description |
|---|---|
| `contains` | Contact must have this tag |
| `containsAny` | Contact must have at least one of these tags |
| `containsAll` | Contact must have all of these tags |

## Properties

Properties are arbitrary key-value data stored on a contact. Use them for structured data that doesn't fit tags.

```json
{
  "properties": {
    "plan": "pro",
    "company": "Acme",
    "signupDate": "2024-01-15",
    "referralSource": "website"
  }
}
```

Properties can be used in audience filters for campaigns:

```json
{
  "audienceFilter": {
    "properties": {
      "plan": "pro"
    }
  }
}
```

Property filters match on exact equality.

## Batch Import

Import up to 1000 contacts in a single request:

```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:3891/v1/contacts/batch \
  -H "x-api-key: pgn_..." \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '[
    {"email": "alice@example.com", "firstName": "Alice", "tags": ["import"]},
    {"email": "bob@example.com", "firstName": "Bob", "tags": ["import"]},
    {"email": "carol@example.com", "firstName": "Carol", "tags": ["import"]}
  ]'
```

```typescript
const result = await pigeons.contacts.batchCreate([
  { email: 'alice@example.com', firstName: 'Alice', tags: ['import'] },
  { email: 'bob@example.com', firstName: 'Bob', tags: ['import'] },
  { email: 'carol@example.com', firstName: 'Carol', tags: ['import'] },
])
// { created: 3, skipped: 0, contacts: [...] }
```

Existing email addresses are silently skipped and counted in the `skipped` field.

## List with Filters

```bash
# List all contacts
curl "http://localhost:3891/v1/contacts" -H "x-api-key: pgn_..."

# Filter by tag
curl "http://localhost:3891/v1/contacts?tag=newsletter" -H "x-api-key: pgn_..."

# Paginate
curl "http://localhost:3891/v1/contacts?limit=50&cursor=2024-01-15T10:30:00.000Z" \
  -H "x-api-key: pgn_..."
```

## Get by ID or Email

Contacts can be retrieved by either their ID (`ctc_...`) or email address:

```bash
# By ID
curl http://localhost:3891/v1/contacts/ctc_abc123... -H "x-api-key: pgn_..."

# By email
curl http://localhost:3891/v1/contacts/alice@example.com -H "x-api-key: pgn_..."
```

The same applies to update, delete, unsubscribe, and resubscribe endpoints.

## Unsubscribe Handling

### Global unsubscribe

Marks the contact as unsubscribed from all emails. Campaigns and sequences skip unsubscribed contacts.

```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:3891/v1/contacts/ctc_abc123.../unsubscribe \
  -H "x-api-key: pgn_..."
```

### Per-topic unsubscribe

Unsubscribe from a specific topic (e.g. "marketing" but not "product-updates"). First create subscription topics, then pass the topic ID:

```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:3891/v1/contacts/ctc_abc123.../unsubscribe \
  -H "x-api-key: pgn_..." \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"topicId": "top_xyz..."}'
```

Campaigns linked to a topic via `topicId` will skip contacts unsubscribed from that topic.

### Resubscribe

```bash
# Global resubscribe
curl -X POST http://localhost:3891/v1/contacts/ctc_abc123.../resubscribe \
  -H "x-api-key: pgn_..."

# Per-topic resubscribe
curl -X POST http://localhost:3891/v1/contacts/ctc_abc123.../resubscribe \
  -H "x-api-key: pgn_..." \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"topicId": "top_xyz..."}'
```

## Automatic Status Tracking

Pigeons automatically updates contact status based on email events:

| Field | Set when |
|---|---|
| `bounced` / `bouncedAt` | SES reports a hard bounce for this contact |
| `complained` / `complainedAt` | SES reports a complaint (spam report) |
| `unsubscribed` / `unsubscribedAt` | Unsubscribe endpoint is called |

Campaigns and sequences automatically exclude contacts where `unsubscribed`, `bounced`, or `complained` is true.


============================================================
Templates (templates)
============================================================

---
title: Templates
description: Create reusable email templates with variables for campaigns and transactional sends.
---

## Create a Template

Templates have a unique slug, a subject line, and an HTML body. Both subject and body support `{{variable}}` interpolation.

```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:3891/v1/templates \
  -H "x-api-key: pgn_..." \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "slug": "welcome-email",
    "name": "Welcome Email",
    "subject": "Welcome, {{name}}!",
    "body": "<h1>Welcome to {{company}}</h1><p>Hi {{name}}, thanks for signing up.</p>",
    "sampleData": {"name": "Alice", "company": "Acme"}
  }'
```

```typescript
const template = await pigeons.templates.create({
  slug: 'welcome-email',
  name: 'Welcome Email',
  subject: 'Welcome, {{name}}!',
  body: '<h1>Welcome to {{company}}</h1><p>Hi {{name}}, thanks for signing up.</p>',
  sampleData: { name: 'Alice', company: 'Acme' },
})
```

### Slug rules

- Lowercase letters, numbers, and hyphens only
- Must be unique across all templates
- Used as a stable identifier in API calls (alternative to `tpl_` IDs)

## Variables

Use `{{variableName}}` in both the subject and body. Variables are replaced with values from the `data` object at send time.

```html
<h1>Welcome to {{company}}</h1>
<p>Hi {{name}},</p>
<p>Your account is ready. Your plan: {{plan}}.</p>
```

Sent with:

```json
{
  "data": {
    "name": "Alice",
    "company": "Acme",
    "plan": "Pro"
  }
}
```

Produces:

```html
<h1>Welcome to Acme</h1>
<p>Hi Alice,</p>
<p>Your account is ready. Your plan: Pro.</p>
```

## Sample Data

The `sampleData` field stores default variable values for previewing the template without passing data:

```json
{
  "sampleData": {
    "name": "Alice",
    "company": "Acme",
    "plan": "Pro"
  }
}
```

This data is used by the preview endpoint and is never sent to real recipients.

## Preview a Template

Render a template without sending:

```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:3891/v1/templates/welcome-email/preview \
  -H "x-api-key: pgn_..." \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"data": {"name": "Bob", "company": "Widgets Inc"}}'
```

If no `data` is provided, the template's `sampleData` is used.

Response:

```json
{
  "subject": "Welcome, Bob!",
  "html": "<h1>Welcome to Widgets Inc</h1>...",
  "text": "Welcome to Widgets Inc..."
}
```

The response includes both HTML and a plain-text version automatically generated from the HTML.

## Using Templates in Sends

### Direct send

Pass the template slug or ID in `templateId`, and variables in `data`:

```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:3891/v1/emails \
  -H "x-api-key: pgn_..." \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "to": "alice@example.com",
    "templateId": "welcome-email",
    "data": {"name": "Alice", "company": "Acme"}
  }'
```

```typescript
const email = await pigeons.emails.send({
  to: 'alice@example.com',
  templateId: 'welcome-email',
  data: { name: 'Alice', company: 'Acme' },
})
```

The subject is rendered from the template. You can override it by passing `subject` explicitly.

### In campaigns

Assign a template to a campaign. The `templateData` provides variables:

```typescript
const campaign = await pigeons.campaigns.create({
  name: 'Product Launch',
  templateId: 'product-launch',
  templateData: { launchDate: '2024-06-01', featureName: 'Dark Mode' },
  audienceFilter: { tags: { contains: 'newsletter' } },
})
```

### In sequences

Each email step in a sequence can reference a template:

```typescript
const sequence = await pigeons.sequences.create({
  name: 'Onboarding',
  steps: [
    { type: 'email', templateId: 'welcome-email', subject: 'Welcome!' },
    { type: 'delay', delayDuration: '1d' },
    { type: 'email', templateId: 'getting-started' },
  ],
})
```

## Lookup by Slug or ID

All template endpoints accept either the `tpl_` prefixed ID or the slug:

```bash
# By slug
curl http://localhost:3891/v1/templates/welcome-email -H "x-api-key: pgn_..."

# By ID
curl http://localhost:3891/v1/templates/tpl_abc123... -H "x-api-key: pgn_..."
```

## Versioning

Templates are automatically versioned. The `version` field starts at 1 and increments when you update the `subject` or `body`. This lets you track changes over time.

```typescript
const updated = await pigeons.templates.update('welcome-email', {
  body: '<h1>New design</h1><p>Hi {{name}}</p>',
})
console.log(updated.version) // 2
```

Updating only `name` or `sampleData` does not increment the version.

## Delete a Template

```bash
curl -X DELETE http://localhost:3891/v1/templates/welcome-email \
  -H "x-api-key: pgn_..."
```

Deleting a template does not affect emails already sent using it.


============================================================
Inboxes (inboxes)
============================================================

---
title: Inboxes
description: Receive email into Pigeons with SES inbound, threading, and webhook delivery.
---

## Overview

Pigeons inboxes let you receive email at real addresses and access messages via API. The inbound pipeline:

1. Someone sends email to `support@yourdomain.com`
2. SES receipt rule saves the raw MIME to S3 and notifies via SNS
3. Pigeons receives the SNS notification, fetches the email from S3, parses it
4. The message is routed to the matching inbox, threaded, and stored
5. Webhooks fire with the `inbox.message.received` event

## Prerequisites

Inbound email requires:

- An AWS region that supports SES inbound (`us-east-1`, `us-west-2`, or `eu-west-1`)
- An S3 bucket for raw MIME storage
- An SNS topic for inbound notifications
- An SES receipt rule routing your domain to S3 + SNS
- An MX record pointing your domain to SES inbound

The easiest way to set all this up is the CLI wizard:

```bash
pigeons setup aws --domain yourdomain.com
```

## Manual SES Setup

### 1. S3 bucket

Create a bucket (e.g. `pigeons-inbound-yourdomain-com`) with a policy allowing SES to write objects:

```json
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [{
    "Sid": "AllowSESPut",
    "Effect": "Allow",
    "Principal": {"Service": "ses.amazonaws.com"},
    "Action": "s3:PutObject",
    "Resource": "arn:aws:s3:::pigeons-inbound-yourdomain-com/*",
    "Condition": {"StringEquals": {"AWS:SourceAccount": "123456789012"}}
  }]
}
```

Set these environment variables:

```
PIGEONS_INBOUND_S3_BUCKET=pigeons-inbound-yourdomain-com
PIGEONS_INBOUND_S3_KEY_PREFIX=inbound/
```

### 2. SNS topic

Create an SNS topic (e.g. `pigeons-inbound-yourdomain-com`) and subscribe it to your Pigeons server:

```bash
aws sns subscribe \
  --topic-arn arn:aws:sns:us-east-1:123456789:pigeons-inbound-yourdomain-com \
  --protocol https \
  --endpoint https://pigeons.yourdomain.com/v1/internal/ses/inbound
```

### 3. SES receipt rule

Create a receipt rule set and rule:

```bash
# Create rule set (one-time)
aws ses create-receipt-rule-set --rule-set-name pigeons-inbound
aws ses set-active-receipt-rule-set --rule-set-name pigeons-inbound

# Create rule for your domain
aws ses create-receipt-rule \
  --rule-set-name pigeons-inbound \
  --rule '{
    "Name": "pigeons-yourdomain-com",
    "Enabled": true,
    "Recipients": ["yourdomain.com"],
    "Actions": [
      {"S3Action": {"BucketName": "pigeons-inbound-yourdomain-com", "ObjectKeyPrefix": "inbound/"}},
      {"SNSAction": {"TopicArn": "arn:aws:sns:us-east-1:123456789:pigeons-inbound-yourdomain-com", "Encoding": "UTF-8"}}
    ],
    "ScanEnabled": true
  }'
```

### 4. MX record

Point your domain to SES inbound:

```
MX  yourdomain.com  →  10 inbound-smtp.us-east-1.amazonaws.com
```

## Create an Inbox

```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:3891/v1/inboxes \
  -H "x-api-key: pgn_..." \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "name": "Support",
    "emailAddress": "support@yourdomain.com",
    "description": "Customer support inbox",
    "webhookUrl": "https://your-app.com/webhooks/email"
  }'
```

```typescript
const inbox = await pigeons.inboxes.create({
  name: 'Support',
  emailAddress: 'support@yourdomain.com',
  webhookUrl: 'https://your-app.com/webhooks/email',
})
```

The `emailAddress` must belong to a domain with inbound capabilities configured.

## Webhook Delivery

When a message arrives, Pigeons fires a webhook to the inbox's `webhookUrl` (if set) and to any globally registered webhooks subscribed to `inbox.message.received`.

Webhook payload:

```json
{
  "event": "inbox.message.received",
  "data": {
    "inbox_id": "inb_abc123...",
    "message_id": "imsg_xyz789...",
    "thread_id": "thr_def456...",
    "from": "customer@example.com",
    "to": ["support@yourdomain.com"],
    "subject": "Help with my order",
    "text": "I need help with order #123...",
    "direction": "inbound"
  }
}
```

## Threading

Pigeons automatically threads messages using email headers:

1. **In-Reply-To** / **References** headers - standard email threading
2. **Subject matching** - messages with the same subject and participants are grouped

Each thread tracks:

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| `id` | Thread ID (`thr_...`) |
| `subject` | Thread subject |
| `lastMessageAt` | Timestamp of the most recent message |
| `messageCount` | Number of messages in the thread |
| `participants` | Array of `{ email, name? }` |
| `status` | `open`, `closed`, or `snoozed` |

### List threads

```bash
curl "http://localhost:3891/v1/inboxes/inb_abc123.../threads?status=open" \
  -H "x-api-key: pgn_..."
```

### Get messages in a thread

```bash
curl "http://localhost:3891/v1/inboxes/inb_abc123.../messages?thread_id=thr_def456..." \
  -H "x-api-key: pgn_..."
```

### Update thread status

```bash
curl -X PATCH http://localhost:3891/v1/inboxes/inb_abc123.../threads/thr_def456... \
  -H "x-api-key: pgn_..." \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"status": "closed"}'
```

## Send from an Inbox

Reply to a message or start a new conversation:

```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:3891/v1/inboxes/inb_abc123.../messages \
  -H "x-api-key: pgn_..." \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "to": "customer@example.com",
    "subject": "Re: Help with my order",
    "html": "<p>Thanks for reaching out. Let me look into order #123.</p>",
    "inReplyTo": "imsg_previous..."
  }'
```

The `inReplyTo` field maintains threading. When set, the outbound message is added to the same thread as the referenced message.

## Reply Extraction

Inbound messages include both the full content and extracted content:

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| `html` | Full HTML body |
| `text` | Full plain text body |
| `extractedHtml` | Just the new reply (quoted text stripped) |
| `extractedText` | Just the new reply as plain text |

Use the `extracted*` fields to show only the new content without quoted reply chains.

## Catch-All Inbox

Designate one inbox as the catch-all to receive messages that don't match any other inbox:

```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:3891/v1/inboxes/inb_abc123.../catch-all \
  -H "x-api-key: pgn_..."
```

Only one inbox can be catch-all at a time. Setting a new catch-all removes the flag from the previous one.

When an inbound email arrives for an address that doesn't match any inbox's `emailAddress`, it routes to the catch-all inbox. If no catch-all is configured, unmatched messages are discarded.

## Pause and Resume

```bash
# Pause - stops accepting new messages
curl -X POST http://localhost:3891/v1/inboxes/inb_abc123.../pause -H "x-api-key: pgn_..."

# Resume
curl -X POST http://localhost:3891/v1/inboxes/inb_abc123.../resume -H "x-api-key: pgn_..."
```

Paused inboxes still receive email at the SES level, but Pigeons does not store or process the messages.

## Message Attachments

Inbound messages with attachments include an `attachments` array:

```json
{
  "attachments": [
    {
      "filename": "invoice.pdf",
      "contentType": "application/pdf",
      "size": 45231,
      "s3Key": "inbound/attachment/..."
    }
  ]
}
```

The `s3Key` can be used to download the attachment from the inbound S3 bucket.


============================================================
Campaigns & Sequences (campaigns)
============================================================

---
title: Campaigns & Sequences
description: Send bulk campaigns to targeted audiences and build multi-step automated sequences.
---

## Campaigns

A campaign sends one email to a set of contacts, filtered by tags and properties.

### Lifecycle

```
draft → sending → sent
         ↓  ↑
        paused

draft → scheduled → sending → sent
                      ↓
                   cancelled
```

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `draft` | Campaign is being configured. Can be edited. |
| `scheduled` | Waiting for `scheduledAt` time. Can be cancelled. |
| `sending` | Actively sending to recipients. Can be paused or cancelled. |
| `paused` | Sending paused. Can be resumed. |
| `sent` | All emails have been processed. |
| `cancelled` | Campaign was cancelled before completing. |

### Create a campaign

```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:3891/v1/campaigns \
  -H "x-api-key: pgn_..." \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "name": "October Newsletter",
    "templateId": "monthly-newsletter",
    "templateData": {"month": "October", "highlight": "New API features"},
    "audienceFilter": {"tags": {"contains": "newsletter"}},
    "fromName": "Acme Updates",
    "fromEmail": "newsletter@yourdomain.com"
  }'
```

```typescript
const campaign = await pigeons.campaigns.create({
  name: 'October Newsletter',
  templateId: 'monthly-newsletter',
  templateData: { month: 'October', highlight: 'New API features' },
  audienceFilter: { tags: { contains: 'newsletter' } },
  fromName: 'Acme Updates',
  fromEmail: 'newsletter@yourdomain.com',
})
```

### Audience Filters

The `audienceFilter` object determines which contacts receive the campaign. Contacts where `unsubscribed`, `bounced`, or `complained` is true are always excluded.

#### Filter by tags

```json
{
  "audienceFilter": {
    "tags": {
      "contains": "newsletter"
    }
  }
}
```

| Operator | Description |
|---|---|
| `contains` | Contact must have this exact tag |
| `containsAny` | Contact must have at least one of these tags |
| `containsAll` | Contact must have all of these tags |

```json
{
  "tags": {
    "containsAll": ["newsletter", "active"],
    "containsAny": ["pro", "enterprise"]
  }
}
```

#### Filter by properties

```json
{
  "audienceFilter": {
    "properties": {
      "plan": "pro",
      "region": "us"
    }
  }
}
```

Properties match on exact equality. All specified properties must match.

#### Combined filters

```json
{
  "audienceFilter": {
    "tags": {"contains": "newsletter"},
    "properties": {"plan": "pro"}
  }
}
```

#### No filter

Omit `audienceFilter` to target all eligible contacts (those not unsubscribed, bounced, or complained).

### Send a campaign

```bash
# Send immediately
curl -X POST http://localhost:3891/v1/campaigns/cmp_abc123.../send \
  -H "x-api-key: pgn_..."

# Schedule for later
curl -X POST http://localhost:3891/v1/campaigns/cmp_abc123.../send \
  -H "x-api-key: pgn_..." \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"scheduledAt": "2024-06-01T09:00:00Z"}'
```

The campaign must have either a `templateId` or a `subject`. When sending, Pigeons:

1. Queries all contacts matching the audience filter
2. Excludes unsubscribed, bounced, and complained contacts
3. Creates a job to send to each eligible contact
4. Updates the `stats.total` field with the audience size

If no eligible contacts match, the send fails with a validation error.

### Pause / Resume / Cancel

```bash
# Pause (only while sending)
curl -X POST http://localhost:3891/v1/campaigns/cmp_abc123.../pause \
  -H "x-api-key: pgn_..."

# Resume (only while paused)
curl -X POST http://localhost:3891/v1/campaigns/cmp_abc123.../resume \
  -H "x-api-key: pgn_..."

# Cancel (while sending or scheduled)
curl -X POST http://localhost:3891/v1/campaigns/cmp_abc123.../cancel \
  -H "x-api-key: pgn_..."
```

### Campaign stats

```typescript
const campaign = await pigeons.campaigns.get('cmp_abc123...')
console.log(campaign.stats)
```

```json
{
  "total": 500,
  "sent": 450,
  "delivered": 440,
  "opened": 120,
  "bounced": 5,
  "complained": 1,
  "failed": 4
}
```

Stats update in real time as SES delivery events arrive. The `opened` count requires [open tracking](/docs/open-tracking) to be enabled.

### Topic-scoped campaigns

Link a campaign to a subscription topic so contacts who unsubscribed from that specific topic are excluded:

```typescript
const campaign = await pigeons.campaigns.create({
  name: 'Marketing Update',
  topicId: 'top_marketing...',
  templateId: 'marketing-update',
  audienceFilter: { tags: { contains: 'active' } },
})
```

---

## Sequences

A sequence is a multi-step automation that sends a series of emails to individual contacts over time.

### Create a sequence

```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:3891/v1/sequences \
  -H "x-api-key: pgn_..." \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "name": "Onboarding",
    "steps": [
      {"type": "email", "templateId": "welcome-email", "subject": "Welcome!"},
      {"type": "delay", "delayDuration": "1d"},
      {"type": "email", "templateId": "getting-started", "subject": "Getting Started"},
      {"type": "delay", "delayDuration": "3d"},
      {"type": "email", "templateId": "tips", "subject": "Pro Tips"}
    ]
  }'
```

### Step types

| Type | Fields | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `email` | `templateId`, `subject`, `templateData`, `topicId` | Sends an email using a template |
| `delay` | `delayDuration` | Waits before proceeding. Format: `30m`, `12h`, `1d`, `7d` |
| `condition` | `condition` | Evaluates a condition before continuing |

### Sequence lifecycle

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `draft` | Being configured. Can't enroll contacts yet. |
| `active` | Running. Contacts can be enrolled. |
| `paused` | Temporarily stopped. Active enrollments are frozen. |
| `archived` | Permanently disabled. |

### Activate a sequence

A sequence must have at least one step before it can be activated:

```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:3891/v1/sequences/seq_abc123.../activate \
  -H "x-api-key: pgn_..."
```

### Enroll a contact

```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:3891/v1/sequences/seq_abc123.../enroll \
  -H "x-api-key: pgn_..." \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"contactId": "ctc_def456..."}'
```

```typescript
const enrollment = await pigeons.sequences.enroll('seq_abc123...', 'ctc_def456...')
console.log(enrollment.status) // "active"
```

The sequence must be `active`. Enrollment creates a job to process the first step.

### Enrollment statuses

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `active` | Currently progressing through steps |
| `completed` | Finished all steps |
| `exited` | Removed early (e.g. unsubscribed) |
| `failed` | A step failed |

### Monitor enrollments

```bash
curl "http://localhost:3891/v1/sequences/seq_abc123.../enrollments?status=active" \
  -H "x-api-key: pgn_..."
```

### Update a sequence

Pause the sequence first, then update:

```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:3891/v1/sequences/seq_abc123.../pause \
  -H "x-api-key: pgn_..."

curl -X PATCH http://localhost:3891/v1/sequences/seq_abc123... \
  -H "x-api-key: pgn_..." \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"steps": [...]}'
```

When steps are provided in an update, the entire step list is replaced.

### Sequence stats

```json
{
  "stats": {
    "enrolled": 150,
    "completed": 80,
    "exited": 10,
    "active": 60
  }
}
```

Per-step stats track `sent`, `delivered`, `opened`, `bounced`, and `complained` for each email step.


============================================================
Webhooks (webhooks)
============================================================

---
title: Webhooks
description: Subscribe to email events and inbound messages with HTTP webhooks.
---

## Overview

Webhooks deliver real-time notifications when events happen in your Pigeons instance. When an event fires, Pigeons sends a POST request to each registered webhook that subscribes to that event type.

## Event Types

| Event | Fires when |
|---|---|
| `email.sent` | An email is accepted by SES |
| `email.delivered` | SES confirms delivery to the recipient |
| `email.bounced` | SES reports a bounce |
| `email.complained` | SES reports a spam complaint |
| `email.opened` | A recipient opens an email (requires open tracking) |
| `email.failed` | An email fails to send |
| `inbox.message.received` | An inbound email arrives at an inbox |
| `inbox.message.sent` | An outbound email is sent from an inbox |
| `contact.created` | A new contact is created |
| `contact.updated` | A contact is updated |
| `contact.unsubscribed` | A contact unsubscribes |
| `campaign.sent` | A campaign email is sent |
| `campaign.completed` | A campaign finishes sending to all recipients |
| `sequence.step.sent` | A sequence step email is sent |

## Create a Webhook

```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:3891/v1/webhooks \
  -H "x-api-key: pgn_..." \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "url": "https://your-app.com/webhooks/pigeons",
    "events": ["email.delivered", "email.bounced", "inbox.message.received"]
  }'
```

```typescript
const webhook = await pigeons.webhooks.create({
  url: 'https://your-app.com/webhooks/pigeons',
  events: ['email.delivered', 'email.bounced', 'inbox.message.received'],
})

console.log(webhook.secret) // "whsec_..." - only returned on creation
```

A signing secret is auto-generated if you don't provide one (minimum 16 characters). The secret is only returned in the create response. Store it securely.

## Payload Format

Every webhook delivery is a POST request with a JSON body:

```json
{
  "event": "email.delivered",
  "data": {
    "email_id": "msg_abc123...",
    "delivered_at": "2024-01-15T10:30:05.000Z"
  }
}
```

### Headers

| Header | Description |
|---|---|
| `Content-Type` | `application/json` |
| `X-Pigeons-Signature` | HMAC-SHA256 signature of the request body |
| `X-Pigeons-Event` | Event type (e.g. `email.delivered`) |
| `X-Pigeons-Delivery` | Unique delivery ID (`wdl_...`) |

### Example payloads

**email.delivered:**

```json
{
  "event": "email.delivered",
  "data": {
    "email_id": "msg_abc123...",
    "delivered_at": "2024-01-15T10:30:05.000Z"
  }
}
```

**email.bounced:**

```json
{
  "event": "email.bounced",
  "data": {
    "email_id": "msg_abc123...",
    "bounce_type": "Permanent",
    "bounced_at": "2024-01-15T10:30:05.000Z"
  }
}
```

**inbox.message.received:**

```json
{
  "event": "inbox.message.received",
  "data": {
    "inbox_id": "inb_abc123...",
    "message_id": "imsg_xyz789...",
    "thread_id": "thr_def456...",
    "from": "customer@example.com",
    "to": ["support@yourdomain.com"],
    "subject": "Help with my order",
    "text": "I need help with order #123...",
    "direction": "inbound"
  }
}
```

**email.opened:**

```json
{
  "event": "email.opened",
  "data": {
    "email_id": "msg_abc123...",
    "opened_at": "2024-01-15T14:22:00.000Z"
  }
}
```

## Signature Verification

Every delivery is signed with your webhook's secret using HMAC-SHA256. Verify signatures to ensure requests come from your Pigeons instance.

### Node.js

```typescript
import { createHmac } from 'crypto'

function verifySignature(body: string, signature: string, secret: string): boolean {
  const expected = createHmac('sha256', secret).update(body).digest('hex')
  return expected === signature
}

// In your webhook handler:
app.post('/webhooks/pigeons', (req, res) => {
  const signature = req.headers['x-pigeons-signature'] as string
  const rawBody = JSON.stringify(req.body)

  if (!verifySignature(rawBody, signature, 'whsec_your_secret')) {
    return res.status(401).send('Invalid signature')
  }

  // Process the event
  const { event, data } = req.body
  console.log(`Received ${event}:`, data)

  res.status(200).send('ok')
})
```

### Python

```python
import hmac
import hashlib

def verify_signature(body: bytes, signature: str, secret: str) -> bool:
    expected = hmac.new(
        secret.encode(),
        body,
        hashlib.sha256,
    ).hexdigest()
    return hmac.compare_digest(expected, signature)
```

## Retry Policy

Failed deliveries are retried with exponential backoff:

| Attempt | Delay |
|---|---|
| 1 | Immediate |
| 2 | 1 minute |
| 3 | 5 minutes |
| 4 (final) | 15 minutes |

A delivery is considered failed if:

- The endpoint returns a non-2xx status code
- The request times out (10 second timeout)
- The connection fails

After 3 retry attempts, the delivery is abandoned.

### Auto-disable

After 10 consecutive failures across any deliveries, the webhook is automatically disabled (status set to `disabled`). Re-enable it by updating the webhook:

```bash
curl -X PATCH http://localhost:3891/v1/webhooks/whk_abc123... \
  -H "x-api-key: pgn_..." \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"status": "active"}'
```

## Manage Webhooks

### List

```bash
curl http://localhost:3891/v1/webhooks -H "x-api-key: pgn_..."
```

The list response does not include secrets.

### Update

```bash
curl -X PATCH http://localhost:3891/v1/webhooks/whk_abc123... \
  -H "x-api-key: pgn_..." \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"events": ["email.delivered", "email.bounced", "email.complained"]}'
```

### Delete

```bash
curl -X DELETE http://localhost:3891/v1/webhooks/whk_abc123... \
  -H "x-api-key: pgn_..."
```

## SSRF Protection

Webhook URLs are validated before every delivery to prevent SSRF attacks. URLs pointing to private IP ranges, localhost, or link-local addresses are rejected.


============================================================
Open Tracking (open-tracking)
============================================================

---
title: Open Tracking
description: Track email opens with a transparent tracking pixel.
---

## How It Works

When open tracking is enabled, Pigeons injects a 1x1 transparent GIF pixel into the HTML body of outgoing emails, just before the closing `</body>` tag:

```html
<img src="https://pigeons.yourdomain.com/v1/t/msg_abc123..."
     alt="" width="1" height="1"
     style="display:none!important;width:1px!important;height:1px!important" />
```

When the recipient's email client loads the image, Pigeons records the open. The pixel endpoint returns the image immediately and processes the open asynchronously, so tracking never delays the response.

## Enabling Open Tracking

Open tracking is **off by default**. Two controls determine whether an email gets a tracking pixel:

### Global: `PIGEONS_OPEN_TRACKING`

Set the environment variable to enable tracking for all emails:

```bash
PIGEONS_OPEN_TRACKING=true
PIGEONS_BASE_URL=https://pigeons.yourdomain.com  # required for pixel URLs
```

Both variables are required. Without `PIGEONS_BASE_URL`, pixels cannot be injected because there is no URL to point them to.

### Per-email: `trackOpens`

Override the global setting for individual emails:

```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:3891/v1/emails \
  -H "x-api-key: pgn_..." \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "to": "alice@example.com",
    "subject": "Your invoice",
    "html": "<h1>Invoice #123</h1>",
    "trackOpens": true
  }'
```

```typescript
const email = await pigeons.emails.send({
  to: 'alice@example.com',
  subject: 'Your invoice',
  html: '<h1>Invoice #123</h1>',
  trackOpens: true,
})
```

The resolution order:

1. If `trackOpens` is explicitly set on the email, use that value
2. Otherwise, use the global `PIGEONS_OPEN_TRACKING` setting
3. Default is `false`

## Open Data

When an email is opened, Pigeons updates these fields on the email record:

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| `openCount` | Total number of times the pixel was loaded |
| `firstOpenedAt` | Timestamp of the first open |
| `lastOpenedAt` | Timestamp of the most recent open |

```typescript
const email = await pigeons.emails.get('msg_abc123...')
console.log(email.openCount)     // 3
console.log(email.firstOpenedAt) // "2024-01-15T10:45:00.000Z"
console.log(email.lastOpenedAt)  // "2024-01-16T08:12:00.000Z"
```

## Webhook Event

The first time an email is opened, Pigeons fires the `email.opened` webhook event:

```json
{
  "event": "email.opened",
  "data": {
    "email_id": "msg_abc123...",
    "opened_at": "2024-01-15T10:45:00.000Z"
  }
}
```

The webhook fires only on the first open, not on subsequent opens of the same email.

## Campaign and Sequence Stats

Open tracking integrates with campaign and sequence statistics:

- **Campaigns**: The `stats.opened` counter increments when a campaign email is first opened
- **Sequences**: Each email step has its own `stats.opened` counter

```json
{
  "stats": {
    "total": 500,
    "sent": 450,
    "delivered": 440,
    "opened": 120,
    "bounced": 5,
    "complained": 1,
    "failed": 4
  }
}
```

## Privacy Considerations

Tracking pixels are a common industry practice, but they raise privacy concerns:

- **Accuracy**: Email clients that block remote images will not trigger opens. Apple Mail Privacy Protection pre-fetches images, which can inflate open counts. Open rates are a directional metric, not an exact count.

- **Transparency**: Consider disclosing tracking in your privacy policy. Some jurisdictions require it.

- **Opt-out**: Use the per-email `trackOpens: false` override to skip tracking for specific emails (e.g. transactional receipts where tracking is inappropriate).

- **Default off**: Pigeons defaults to tracking disabled globally. Enable it deliberately when you need the data.

## Tracking Pixel Endpoint

```
GET /v1/t/:emailId
```

This endpoint is unauthenticated (no API key required) and returns a 1x1 transparent GIF with aggressive no-cache headers. It is designed to be embedded in emails and loaded by email clients.

The endpoint responds immediately with the pixel image. Open recording happens asynchronously after the response is sent, so any failures in recording do not affect the pixel response.
